sections.h2: Why does San Angelo's history matter to a home seller?
sections.html:
San Angelo is the Tom Green County seat, set where the North, Middle and South Concho rivers meet in the middle of the state, and its economy rests on military, education, medical and ranching employers that keep housing demand local.

The Texas State Historical Association says the town began in the late 1860s across the North Concho River from Fort Concho, which opened in 1867. The Santa Fe Railroad arrived in 1888, and cattle, sheep, wool and mohair made it a major regional market. Oil from the Permian Basin boom of the 1920s and the 1940 selection of the town for Goodfellow Air Field pushed the population from 10,050 in 1920 to 52,093 by 1950. It stood at 88,439 in 2000.

  • Goodfellow began as an air field in 1940 and later became an Air Force intelligence training base.
  • Angelo State University grew out of San Angelo College, founded in 1928.
  • Shannon Medical Center and other hospitals give the city a health care base.

sections.h2: How can I sell a San Angelo house fast?
sections.html:
Pick between a retail listing, a sale by owner and an as-is cash offer, and weigh how soon you need money against how much price you will give up.

A listing with an agent exposes your house to the full market, which helps if the roof, systems and cosmetics are sound. It also brings buyer financing, an appraisal and repair negotiation. A cash offer from an investor removes most of those steps and can close on your timeline, but it will come in below a polished listing price.

  • Ask each buyer how long closing takes and who pays recording and title charges.
  • Request the offer in writing before you stop marketing the house.
  • Keep copies of the contract and any repair credits agreed.

sections.h2: Where do I look up San Angelo property tax records?
sections.html:
Start with the Tom Green County Appraisal District, which publishes a searchable account and tax summary tab for each parcel.

The district's site explains that after you open your account, the Tax Summary tab shows any amount due and links to online payment by electronic check or credit card. The district also posted May 15, 2026 at midnight as the protest deadline for many residential properties, and told owners to check their Notice of Appraised Value for the exact date on their parcel. Protests can be emailed, postmarked, dropped off or filed on the website. Business personal property filers have a separate email address for rendition forms.

sections.h2: What are the Texas tax dates for a San Angelo owner?
sections.html:
The key dates fall on January 1, May 15, October 1 and January 31, with a split payment option for those who want to pay in two parts.

Texas tax calendar entries relevant to Tom Green County owners (Texas Comptroller)
DateStep
January 2 to April 15Rendition period for most property types
April 1Notices for single-family homesteads mailed, or soon after
July 25Appraisal roll certified to taxing units
October 1Tax bills mailed
November 30First half due under the split option
June 30Second half due under the split option

More detail is on the Comptroller deadlines page.

sections.h2: What happens if San Angelo property taxes go unpaid?
sections.html:
Unpaid taxes become delinquent on February 1 and the lien follows the property to any buyer, so you must clear or arrange them before closing.

The collector adds a six percent penalty and one percent interest at the start, then one percent a month, and a 12 percent penalty from July 1. Interest does not stop at a cap. An attorney retained by the taxing unit can add as much as 20 percent. If you suffered a hardship, a written request for a waiver may be possible when the tax is paid within 21 days of learning about the delinquency. After enough delay, the unit can sue and sell the property at a tax sale. A former owner has two years to claim excess sale proceeds.

  • Pay the oldest year first when the collector accepts partial payments.
  • Homestead owners may qualify for a payment plan of up to 36 months.

sections.h2: Which exemptions can help a San Angelo homeowner?
sections.html:
The homestead exemption is the main one, and owners 65 or older or disabled can add more.

School districts must exclude $140,000 of homestead value and an extra $60,000 for owners 65 or older or disabled. Counties with farm-to-market or flood control taxes give $3,000. A school tax ceiling can freeze the school levy for older or disabled homeowners. The ceiling may follow you to a new Texas homestead in proportion. A buyer who purchases after January 1 can claim the exemption for the rest of the year if the seller did not. A disabled veteran may qualify for between $5,000 and $12,000 off value depending on rating, and at 100 percent for a total exemption on the homestead.

sections.h2: What if tenants live in my San Angelo house?
sections.html:
You can sell with a tenant in place, but if the lease will not carry over you must follow Texas eviction steps before the buyer can take possession.

A landlord generally gives at least three days' written notice to vacate unless the lease says otherwise, then files in justice court. Trial is set within 10 to 21 days after filing and the tenant is served at least four days before. Either side may appeal to county court within five days of judgment. A writ of possession cannot issue until six days after judgment, and the constable gives 24 hours' notice before removal.

sections.h2: How do I sell an inherited house in San Angelo?
sections.html:
Start by finding out whether the owner left a will, because that decides which court paper the buyer's title company will want to see.

Texas allows a will to be probated within four years of death, normally in the county where the owner lived. Where no debts remain except liens on real estate, a muniment of title can carry the house to heirs, and the order plus the will are filed with the county clerk where the land sits. A small estate affidavit works only when there is no will, no administration, and assets of $75,000 or less excluding the homestead and exempt property. An affidavit of heirship is a sworn statement that no law requires a buyer or lender to accept.

  • Gather the death certificate and any recorded deed.
  • Ask the appraisal district what the heirs must file to keep a homestead exemption.
  • Talk to a probate attorney before signing a purchase contract.

sections.h2: What if I am facing foreclosure in San Angelo?
sections.html:
Sell before the auction if you want to keep any equity, since a Texas power-of-sale foreclosure moves on a fixed schedule.

After you receive a notice of default you have 20 days to reinstate by paying what is past due. The notice of sale must then arrive at least 21 days before an auction held on the first Tuesday of the month at the county courthouse area designated by the commissioners court. Any money left after the lenders are paid goes to junior lienholders first and then to you. If the sale price falls short of the debt, a lender has two years to file for a deficiency.

faqs.q: What county is San Angelo in?
faqs.a: Tom Green County. San Angelo is the county seat, and the Tom Green County Appraisal District holds the property records.

faqs.q: Can I pay San Angelo property tax online?
faqs.a: The Tom Green County Appraisal District site shows a link on the Tax Summary page to pay by electronic check or credit card. Confirm current options with the tax office.

faqs.q: Do I need to pay property taxes before I sell?
faqs.a: Any unpaid tax is settled at closing from your proceeds, since the lien stays with the property. Ask for a tax certificate first.

faqs.q: How soon can I get a protest hearing?
faqs.a: Hearings begin after the protest filing deadline, around mid May, and the appraisal review board must approve the roll by July 20. File on time to keep that right.

faqs.q: What does a cash buyer pay for in San Angelo?
faqs.a: Terms vary by buyer, so ask for the offer in writing and read who pays title, recording and any repairs before you sign.
